Theme

log noun

a piece of a tree trunk

also logs, firewood, a log for the fire, tree trunk

classical

Caes. BG 7.73 (Lewis & Short)
Ov. Fast. 5.506: ignis in hesternō stīpite parvus erat

stīpes, stīpitis m.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

a log, a stake, a tree trunk

A log or a post, cut or lying; also, like English “blockhead”, an insult for a dull person (Ter. Heaut. 5.1.4: caudex, stīpes, asinus).

Other words

  • ligna, lignōrum n. pl. — firewood, logs for burning

    noun, second declension, plural · also used · classical · Hor. C. 1.9.5–6; Cic. Verr. 2.1.69: ligna et sarmenta circumdare (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    In this sense classically only plural; lignum is wood as a material (see wood), and timber for building is māteria.

  • truncus, truncī m. — a tree trunk

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 3.179 (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    The trunk of a tree, standing or felled; also the trunk of the body.

Examples

  • dissolve frīgus ligna super focō largē repōnēns

    melt the cold away, piling logs on the hearth without stintHor. C. 1.9.5–6

  • ignis in hesternō stīpite parvus erat

    there was a small fire in yesterday’s logOv. Fast. 5.506

  • Quaerendus cuneus est malus truncō malō.

    a hard log needs a hard wedgePs.-Publ. Q 3

See also wood, woodshed, axe, beam, log in, log out.
